info.title: OpenAsy WAF API
info.description: Sites behind the web application firewall, the OWASP Core Rule Set they run in Coraza, exclusions, custom rules, and the requests the rules matched (ADR 0069).

tags.name: Sites
tags.description: Host names, upstreams, mode and how the rule set runs.

tags.name: Tuning
tags.description: Exclusions for false positives and rules of your own.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Requests the rules matched, and every request counted.

post.description: Needs the admin role. It starts in detection-only mode unless mode says otherwise, and is served at once.

put.description: Needs the admin role. Such as turning blocking on. It takes effect at once.

delete.description: Needs the admin role. Its host names are no longer served; its exclusions and rules go, its events stay until the retention.

post.description: Needs the editor role. For a false positive: a rule, or one target of it, left out on a site, everywhere or under a path.
Needs the editor role. Checked, compiled by Coraza, then served at once, after the rule set.
Needs the editor role. Checks and compiles SecLang without keeping it.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Its request rules as Coraza compiled them, by group and paranoia level, with how often each matched in the last 24 hours.
Needs the viewer role. Newest first.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: One or more of blocked, detected and logged, separated by commas.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the client address, path, query or message, a rule id or an event id.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back. 24h when left out.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: From next of the page before.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many, 1 to 500. 100 when left out.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. By the reference the blocked client was shown.
Needs the viewer role. Every request over the range in buckets, with the attacks, rules and clients matched most.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back. 24h when left out.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. The proxy's state, the sites by mode and the last 24 hours.

200.description: From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.

get.description: Ready while the database answers and the proxy serves the rules last saved.

503.description: The database or the proxy is unavailable.

200.description: Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when WAF runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the WAF origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_waf_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when WAF is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

running.description: The proxy, Coraza with the Core Rule Set, is running.

loaded.description: It serves the rules last saved.

lastError.description: Why it did not take the last rules, or stopped.

dropped.description: Reports of matched requests not kept, because more came than could be written.

hosts.description: Host names without the port, each on one site only. `*` takes every host no other site names.

upstream.description: The application, http:// or https://, without a user or password.

mode.description: detection: rules match and are reported, nothing is refused. New sites start here.

paranoia.description: The rule set's paranoia level: higher catches more and blocks more real users.

inboundThreshold.description: The anomaly score at which a request is blocked. 5 is one critical match.

disabledGroups.description: Groups of the rule set turned off, for a stack the site does not run, such as 933 for PHP.

SiteChange.description: What it names changes; the rest stays.

ruleId.description: A rule's id or a range of ids.

target.description: Only this part of the request, such as ARGS:filter; null for the whole rule.

path.description: Only under this path; null for the whole site.

target.description: ARGS, ARGS_GET, ARGS_POST, REQUEST_COOKIES, REQUEST_HEADERS, REQUEST_FILENAME and the like, with a :name. Only with one ruleId, not a range.

disruptive.description: Of its rules, the ones that refuse a request (deny or drop).

hits24h.description: Requests its rules matched in the last 24 hours. In lists only.

siteId.description: Leave out or null for every site.

seclang.description: SecRule and SecAction only, with ids from 1000000 to 1999999, in phase 1 or 2. Operators that read files, look up DNS or run scripts, and the actions ctl, exec, setenv, allow and redirect are refused.
examples: SecRule ARGS:q "@detectSQLi" "id:1000318,phase:2,deny,status:403,log,msg:'Virtual patch: SQL injection in q'"

RuleChange.description: What it names changes; the rest stays.

paranoia.description: The level from which it runs.

value.description: What matched; for a parameter that names a secret, only its length.

id.description: The reference a blocked client was shown.

query.description: Values of parameters that name a secret are left out.

action.description: blocked; detected: it would have been blocked, the site is in detection-only mode; logged: a rule matched below the threshold.

score.description: The rule set's inbound anomaly score.

attack.description: sqli, xss, lfi, rce, protocol, ... from the rule's tags; custom for rules of your own.

next.description: Pass as cursor for the next page.
